BootyOrbiter did a phenomenal job laying out the science and mathematics of weight maintenance.

I'd like to back this up with a plan that leverages modern electronics (assuming you have smart phone, internet, and all the other common things).

  1. Buy a fitness tracker. FitBit is just one one example.
  2. Install the app for the tracker on your smart phone.
  3. Also install a calorie tracker like MyFitnessPal.
  4. Configure both apps to share data (they each have different strengths).
  5. Set a weight loss goal in the apps. They will calculate TDEE and a calorie plan for you. Since you're young and fit, you don't have to set a particularly challenging goal.
  6. Attempt to get 10,000 steps every day. This is in addition (or in combination) with working out with weights, running, taking a fitness class, or working out with a physical trainer. Point is simply be active.
  7. Count calories, and count them all. You quickly learn exactly what you're eating (both calories and nutrients) and weed out the high calorie / low nutrient foods and replace them with what you should be eating.

I've found by simply following the above, weight maintenance becomes very easy to manage. It really is all about eat less, move more. Electronics make it even easier for me.
